analysis.title: GS Basics: Supportive Micro. Deposit Competition. Downside Growth Risk (27 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Overnight US rebound carried into the broader tech tape: Hynix +5%, Samsung +4%, KOSPI +3%. Privorotsky asks whether this is an oversold bounce in QQQ or the start of something more sustainable.
The week ahead of major political events, with this much risk premium already embedded, tends to be constructive. The market struggles to go down even though people remain reluctant to add risk.

Gulf diplomacy is the main energy focus: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani delegations are in Tehran and Qatar is mediating. Privorotsky sees nothing substantive and says the odds of a breakthrough remain low. Oil has come off Friday's escalatory highs but reversed higher during the session.

If there is no tangible progress by Thursday morning, Privorotsky expects a climb back up the escalatory ladder into the weekend. The market will stay skeptical that much happens before next week's political events.

HSBC fell 5.6% in Hong Kong and set a difficult tone for banks. Increased deposit competition in the UK and Hong Kong contributed to net interest income (NII) compression. Privorotsky flags this as something to watch in Europe more broadly, alongside the lingering threat of agentic capital allocation.
Neoclouds were under pressure after Elon's comments on financing and consolidation. AI credit spreads came off Friday's wides, but AI credit remains the most important thing to watch.

At this point in the cycle, AI is increasingly about the market's willingness to supply capital and at what price. The cost of capital has risen materially, which is changing the economics of the whole complex. Any sustained relief in credit should be a powerful catalyst.

Privorotsky raises the possibility that the sheer scale of AI spending eventually drives excess compute capacity, structurally lower returns and lower multiples. He calls this unclear, with theoretical debate about oversupply into 2027/28.

AI micro remains robust. Celestica rose about 17% aftermarket after a comfortable beat and guidance to $40bn of 2027 revenue, up 90% YoY, with 2028 demand indications stronger. This is a positive read-through for networking and optical.
Cadence beat and raised, with $8.2bn of backlog and strong AI-driven design demand. Rambus also beat but slipped after the close.
Demand is not the problem today. The debate is how much to discount future cash flows given uncertainty around supply, competition and financing.

Front-end rates have stabilized, which Privorotsky calls objectively good for risk. Energy is too high for comfort but is more likely to produce chop than a sustained selloff absent another escalation.
Credit is the main worry, still flashing yellow to red relative to equities. If credit calms, Privorotsky thinks it could be a meaningful catalyst for a broader rally.

Hyperscaler earnings and the Fed are the main events this week. Four focus items: capex (flat or up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks and shovels), backlog conversion into revenue, free cash flow conversion in the out quarters, and financing (equity versus debt).

Flows were a little more supportive: after weeks of net selling of tech, clients showed demand on the other side, at least in Europe. The modal view is that markets chop until next week's political events clear.
